business_scope.primary_industry_name: Precision Heavy-Load Polymer-Modified Bitumen Runway Laying

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with a separate administrative law branch and EU-derived commercial legislation; notary system integrated
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France's network of extra-EU bilateral investment treaties maintained under Regulation (EU) No 1219/2012
France's worldwide double taxation agreement network, including more than 130 instruments in force
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applicable to France
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (2019), applicable to France

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq., as amended by Sapin II Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Article L.561-45 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier and Decree No. 2014-1462 of 4 December 2014 establishing the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; French Commercial Code, Articles L.123-123 and R.123-214 et seq. for the filing of the beneficial owner declaration with the registre du commerce et des sociétés via the Guichet Unique, coordinated by INPI

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of each non-French shareholder (extrait du registre des sociétés / certificate of good standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate articles or by-laws of each non-French corporate shareholder, evidencing corporate capacity and approval of the French incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, board of directors, or equivalent officer of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille or French consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or sole shareholder decision authorizing the incorporation of the French SARL, the subscription of capital, and the appointment of the gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors or equivalent governing body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in origin and apostilled or consularly legalized as appropriate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the French legal representative or notaire for signature of the statuts, UBO declaration, and registry filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each beneficial owner or corporate shareholder authorized to sign
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of execution and Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed shareholders, UBOs, managers and attorneys-in-fact against the French TRACFIN guidance, EU Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001, EU Regulation 269/2014, the consolidated EU terrorist list, UN Security Council sanctions, and, where a US nexus exists, OFAC SDN/restricted lists. The protocol requires: (i) identification of every UBO holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights through nominal ownership, chain control, bearer instruments or other control mechanisms; (ii) verification of PEP status under Article R.561-17 of the Code monétaire et financier for foreign politically exposed persons and their family members/close associates; (iii) enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions and non-transparent ownership structures; (iv) written evidence of source of funds and business rationale for the French runway asphalt-laying contracting activity; and (v) retention of the AML/CFT file for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce, accessed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability may be pre-screened through INPI Data (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be expressed in Latin characters and French orthography. All statutory documents, the articles of association, registry filings and the name application must be in French. Foreign script transliteration into Latin characters is accepted for ancillary trading names, but the legal name and legal-form suffix 'SARL' must remain French and clearly stated in all deeds and commercial documents. The name may not be misleading as to the legal form, object, or public status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banking and financial-services reserved words: 'banque', 'crédit', 'société de financement', 'assurance', 'mutuelle', 'fiduciaire', 'courtier', 'change', unless authorized by the ACPR
State and public-authority tokens: 'République', 'État', 'France' used in a manner implying official capacity, 'mairie', 'préfecture', 'ministère', 'police', 'gendarmerie'
Regulated-profession terms: 'avocat', 'notaire', 'expert-comptable', 'commissaire aux comptes', 'médecin', 'pharmacien', 'architecte' without the relevant professional authorization
Civil-aviation public-establishment identifiers such as 'Aéroports de Paris' or misleading similarity to 'DGAC' (Direction générale de l'aviation civile)
Words contrary to public order, morality, or foreign sovereign insignia, and names falsely suggesting a public concession or monopoly in airport infrastructure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no separate statutory name-reservation register distinct from the RCS filing; therefore the official name-clearance result is treated as provisionally valid for 30 operational days. If the filing is not completed within that window, the availability check may be renewed without additional ministerial formality. If the Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant may correct the dossier and resubmit through the Guichet Unique, or file a judicial challenge before the commercial court under Articles R.123-24-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code where the registrar's refusal is alleged to be unlawful. Where rejection rests on prior trademark rights, the applicant may obtain a letter of consent from the earlier owner, commence trademark cancellation or opposition proceedings before INPI, or file a civil action before the French courts for infringement or nullity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or licensed business-center domiciliation may serve as the French registered office only through a legally authorized domiciliation company under Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-16-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. The arrangement must be evidenced by a written contract, the legal records and social/accounting documents must remain accessible at the domiciled address, and French tax and registry authorities must be able to contact management there. For an airport runway asphalt-paving contractor, a virtual office cannot replace the physical establishment, equipment yard or safety-management location required by the civil aviation contract and public procurement rules. A separate declared operating establishment in France will ordinarily be required for DGAC and site-safety inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high quantified risk of approximately 35% in the first three years from tax, social security (URSSAF), trade inspectorate, or corporate registry verification visits. The likelihood increases to 60-70% for airport-runway contractors because the Direction générale de l'aviation civile, the contracting airport authority and the civil aviation safety inspectorate may conduct unannounced site, equipment, quality-control, and asphalt mix/polymer certification inspections at short notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name availability and French trademark clearance search covering classes 19, 37 and relevant aviation-related goods/services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French counsel / INPI Data commercial search provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for pre-incorporation due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the French SARL articles of association, shareholder documentation and gérant appointment resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per engagement; fixed fee for standard SARL with foreign corporate shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation and apostille/consular legalization of foreign shareholder corporate documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator, French notary and originating consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark plus regulated notarial disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and filing of the beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) with the RCS through the Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French counsel and Greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market legal fee plus statutory filing component included in the registry fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique / RCS incorporation filing fee, droit de greffe and related registry formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under French commercial and registry fee regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal announcement in an authorized legal gazette (insertion d'une annonce légale) for the constitution of the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized by the competent court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-line cap fixed by decree for paid legal announcements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation / registered office service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for licensed business-center domiciliation in France

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of a French business bank account and issuance of the deposit certificate for the SARL share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank tariff for professional account opening and attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening, AML/CFT risk assessment and due diligence file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French counsel and automated AML screening provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional notarial deed for the articles of association, where a French notaire is requested by lenders or civil-aviation procurement counterparties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff plus emoluments, disbursements and VAT

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; French Commercial Code implementing Decree n° 2023-292 of 17 April 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed electronically through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'une société (Cerfa n° 16309*02) accompanied by the signed Statuts (Articles of Association), filed via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 1 (Art. L.223-2, Code de commerce). Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked French bank account or with a notaire/Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the company is registered. If share capital exceeds EUR 5,000, at least 20% of each cash contribution must be paid up at incorporation and the balance within 5 years; if capital is EUR 5,000 or less, all cash contributions must be fully paid upon subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

The founding members, having signed the Statuts, unanimously resolve:

1. That the share capital of EUR [ ] is fully subscribed and distributed as per the Statuts.
2. That the registered office be established at [address], France.
3. That Mr/Ms [Name] is appointed Gérant for the company’s entire duration.
4. That the Gérant may open bank accounts, sign airport paving contracts, and undertake all lawful acts.
5. That all formation fees, duties, and publication charges be borne by the company.
6. That the Gérant be authorized to complete all registration formalities.

The resolution is effective upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders under private deed; optional notaire when contributions include real estate or registered assets (Art. L.223-2, C. com.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French containing mandatory legal provisions: corporate form (SARL), registered name, duration (up to 99 years), registered office address, corporate purpose covering airport runway construction and polymer-modified bitumen paving, share capital and share allocation, management powers of the Gérant, and decision-making rules. All shareholders must sign the Statuts; each signature is authenticated. If a contribution in kind relates to real property, the deed must be notarized.
required_dossiers: Original signed Statuts
Valid identity documents of all shareholders
Draft capital and share allocation schedule
Notarial deed if any real estate contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notaire or registry questions a contribution valuation, amend the Statuts and obtain all shareholder signatures on the revised version before re-submitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscribe and deposit the share capital in a blocked account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; notary for cash escrow when a notarial deed is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary historical-French bank account in the company's formation name. Each shareholder transfers the subscribed cash amount into this blocked account. The bank issues an attestation de dépôt de fonds certifying the deposited capital, the names of the subscribers, and the blocking condition until presentation of the RCS certificate of registration. If the capital comprises contributions in kind, obtain a valuation report from a commissaire aux apports unless all shareholders unanimously waive the audit under the legal exception for small capital and clear value.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Shareholder transfer receipts or SWIFT confirmations
Commissaire aux apports valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit pending further KYC, supply the requested compliance documents or transfer funds to a notaire's escrow account and obtain a notarial blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a statutory formation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed French legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the département where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the formal 'avis de constitution' in French. The notice must contain the intended SARL name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose (including references to ISIC 4210 road and airport runway construction), duration, date of signature of the Statuts, and the appointed Gérant. Send the text electronically to the JAL provider, pay the publication fee, and obtain the official certificate of publication with the notice number.
required_dossiers: Full text of the statutory announcement
Copy of the Statuts signature page
Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the text due to inconsistent or incomplete information, correct the wording and republish. Any additional fee is charged only when a new publication date is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises – INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the file is transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration of the RNE entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the official portal and select the procedure 'création d'une société commerciale'. Complete the dynamic form, upload all required files, sign electronically, and pay the integration fee (taxe de greffe). The Guichet Unique performs an automated completeness check, forwards the file to the registry of the relevant commercial court, and issues a receipt with a dossier number. The registry examines the legality and conformity of the Statuts and annexes before entering the company in the RNE.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts
Bank blocking certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Journal d'Annonces Légales publication certificate
Proof of authorized use of the registered office address
M4 or M3 declaration of the Gérant (or equivalent)
Copy of the Gérant's identity document
Unofficial criminal record / swiss (bulletin n°3) statement for the Gérant
AML/KYC declarations required by the INPI platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a query or a zero-defect hold, the applicant receives a notification through the Guichet Unique with a 15-day term to correct and resubmit the affected documents. If the filing is rejected, an appeal may be lodged before the president of the commercial court in référé.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive the Kbis extract, SIREN and VAT registration proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RNE through the INPI platform; INSEE for statistical identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry approves the incorporation, the Guichet Unique sends an e-mail with a link to download the official Extrait Kbis, the SIREN/SIRET numbers, and the APE code (4210Z - Construction of roads and highways or similar). The file also automatically flows to the tax administration for VAT allocation. Verify on the official French tax portal (entreprendre.service-public.fr) that the intra-community VAT number is active and confirms the identity of the company.
required_dossiers: No additional document – the Kbis and VAT certificate are auto-generated from the approved incorporation file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis or VAT certificate is not made available within 15 calendar days, contact the INPI support desk with the dossier number. For an erroneous APE or address, file a 'mise à jour' request via the same Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt corporate governance instruments and first-management resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's constitutive corporate assembly (founding shareholders acting as governing body)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive general meeting, adopt the first board resolution (as set out in this dossier), confirm the appointment of the Gérant, fix the registered office, and approve the initial accounting year. Have all shareholders sign the meeting minutes and record entry into the corporate register. Deliver a copy of the minutes and the resolution to the bank and to external counterparties. Without changing the registered office, file any subsequent change of management through the Mise à Jour procedure.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution and minutes
Copies of acceptance by the appointed Gérant
Statutory register book (registre des décisions) and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or a counter-party requests a certified extract of the Gérant's authority, obtain an official letter from the registry or a notarized copy of the minutes. In case of registry rejection of a management change, re-file using the 'formalités de mentions modificatives' process within the required deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC), the local Préfecture de police (for civil aviation security), and the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis de travaux sur les zones/mouvements aéroportuaires (Airside Works Permit), issued by the airport operator under the supervision of the DGAC pursuant to the applicable Civil Aviation Regulations (Réglementation de l'Aviation Civile, section 'Travaux' and the airport safety programme).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires – DREAL, Inspection des Installations Classées; with the required permit for wastewater and air emissions issued at the regional level
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration (Déclaration) under ICPE nomenclature Règlementation des installations classées, rubrique 2515 (mobile asphalt concrete mixing units) and relevant fuel/lubricant storage quantities; full environmental impact assessment (Étude d'Impact Environnemental) is mandatory only if the project creates a permanent installation, affects a Natura 2000 site, or runs for more than 12 months at the same location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from asphalt contact surfaces: pH 6–8.5, TSS ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 90 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 5 mg/L (French arrêté of 2 February 1998 and ICPE sectoral standards). Atmospheric emissions: total VOC ≤ 50 mg/m³ expressed as carbon, dust (PM10) ≤ 20 mg/m³, and odour impact as verified by monitoring. Waste management: non-hazardous asphalt/bituminous mixtures (European Waste Catalogue 17 03 02) must be recycled; tar-containing asphalt (17 03 01*) is hazardous and must go to a licensed treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for fuel storage, hot works, and temporary site installations; structural and stability clearance of site cabins, scaffolding, and heavy machinery lifting systems (VGP inspection) by an accredited body; occupational health clearance under the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques (DUERP) and Code du travail, including a medical fitness statement for East airside personnel; security screening for crews working in airport security restricted areas as required by the airport operator.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP); online tax procedures are available through impots.gouv.fr and the professional tax account (espace professionnel). Business formation is filed through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SARL through the INPI Guichet unique to obtain its SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET numbers. Apply to the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) for the French VAT number, generally formed as FR plus a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign business with no French establishment that makes taxable supplies in France must register with the competent non-resident business tax service before or when taxable activity begins; EU-established businesses generally do not need a fiscal representative, while businesses established outside the EU generally must appoint an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable exception or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. French VAT registration does not itself establish a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Certain qualifying family-owned SARLs may elect partnership treatment without the ordinary time limit while eligibility continues. Other qualifying newly formed SARLs may elect partnership treatment for up to five financial years, subject to statutory ownership, activity, size, and timing conditions. France has no general US-style check-the-box election. French and EU anti-hybrid-mismatch rules may deny deductions or require inclusion where classification mismatches produce deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base), the general services threshold is EUR 37,500 of prior-year turnover, with a EUR 41,250 current-year tolerance; the corresponding general goods threshold is EUR 85,000, with a EUR 93,500 tolerance. These thresholds are not a general exemption for foreign suppliers and do not displace registration obligations arising from particular transactions. A French-established contractor exceeding the applicable threshold, or electing to charge VAT, must account for VAT. Construction work on French immovable property is generally located in France; for qualifying B2B supplies by a non-established supplier, the customer may account for VAT under the domestic reverse-charge rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices, and large and intermediate-sized businesses must issue them; SMEs and microbusinesses are scheduled to issue from 1 September 2027. In-scope invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire) or the public invoicing portal, subject to applicable rules. France does not generally operate a real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping system for ordinary VAT invoices. Cross-border transactions and transactions outside the domestic B2B e-invoicing scope may be subject to e-reporting rather than e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be zero-rated when statutory conditions are met and the supplier retains reliable evidence that the goods physically left the EU. Intra-EU supplies are generally exempt with credit (zero-rated) only where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are dispatched there, and the supplier satisfies reporting and evidentiary requirements. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or payment is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. Services directly connected with French immovable property, including runway paving, are generally located where the property is situated; services supplied on a French airport runway are therefore generally subject to French VAT unless a specific exemption or reverse-charge rule applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For goods exported outside the EU: export customs declaration and MRN with electronic exit confirmation or other accepted evidence of exit from the EU customs territory.
Commercial invoice, contract or purchase order, packing list where applicable, and transport evidence such as bill of lading, CMR, air waybill, or carrier confirmation.
For intra-EU supplies: customer VAT identification evidence, transport evidence, and required recapitulative statement and VAT return reporting.
For services: contract, customer and project-location evidence, VAT-status checks, and records substantiating the applicable place-of-supply or exemption rule.

Bank remittance evidence may support the commercial audit trail but is not a general statutory prerequisite for French export zero-rating; France does not generally require an inward remittance certificate.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Unsupported or ineligible zero-rating may result in assessment of output VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and tax surcharges, generally 10% for specified filing or payment failures, 40% for deliberate failure, and up to 80% for fraud or specified concealment, subject to the facts and statutory rules. Fraudulent conduct may also trigger criminal sanctions. The administration may deny input VAT deductions or refund claims and recover amounts previously refunded, with interest and applicable penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully convertible euro currency regime aligned with EU and OECD standards. Both capital and current account transactions face no prior approval or quantitative restrictions. Profit remittances by SARL entities are permitted without limitation when supported by verifiable trade documentation, director declarations, and standard KYC/AML verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export of construction services including runway paving contracts does not trigger mandatory surrender or forced conversion requirements. Repatriation of service proceeds must occur within 12 months for corporate tax and VAT declaration purposes. Voluntary conversion to euro is standard; all transfers require matching invoices, delivery proofs, and purpose codes to satisfy French tax authorities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border EMIs such as Wise Business or Revolut Business are viable for inbound remittances but constrained by French law requiring local banking partner integration for EUR clearing and full compliance with AMF and ACPR regulations. Offshore digital EMIs must route final settlements through regulated French correspondent banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors or signatories is not mandatory for standard SARL corporate account opening. Remote KYC via video identification, digital signatures, and e-KYC platforms is permitted under French Banking Federation guidelines provided the entity holds a valid French SIREN registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds exceeding contract value
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed construction contracts, client purchase orders, proof of project milestones, director beneficial ownership certificates, and source-of-funds letters

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent high-value inbound wires from non-EU entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements, transfer pricing studies, evidence of legitimate trade flows, and ongoing transaction monitoring reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with purpose codes 'CAP' or 'CON'. Beneficiary details must match SARL SIREN registration and director KYC. Non-EU inflows route through correspondent banks with full documentation including board resolutions and capital injection agreements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for project disbursements. All runway paving payments require matching purchase orders, invoices, delivery certificates, and retention release documents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Turnover Declaration (Déclaration de Chiffre d'Affaires - DCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of unreported turnover per month of delay, maximum 25% of turnover; non-filing may result in administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return (Déclaration de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 31 March for calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 0.5% per month of tax due; repeated non-compliance may trigger tax reassessment and company dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Bilan and Compte de Résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and potential judicial dissolution for failure to file accounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or balance sheet total exceeds €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual beneficial owners declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with tax authorities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0-500 USD (registered office at director residence; professional agent services 100-500 USD)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-5000 USD (audit required above thresholds; typical certified audit fee range)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% individual ownership conditions. Certain qualifying businesses established in designated geographic zones may benefit from partial or full corporate income tax exemptions for limited periods. The French research tax credit, innovation tax credit where available, accelerated depreciation, and sector-specific investment incentives may reduce the effective tax burden but do not reduce the headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration de résultats); filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal, impots.gouv.fr, using EDI-TDFC or the approved online filing interface. The return is accompanied by the applicable tax package, including Forms 2058-A, 2058-B, 2058-C, 2058-F, 2059-A through 2059-G, and balance-sheet and profit-and-loss schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with corporate income tax instalments generally paid quarterly through Forms 2571-SD and an annual balance payment through Form 2572-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second business day following 1 May of the following year. A newly incorporated company may have a specific filing deadline based on its first accounting period. Corporate income tax instalments are generally due by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions. The final balance is generally due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following the financial year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year beginning and ending dates, legal form, and accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder must not be substituted for the French SARL. Report the French entity's legal identity and French permanent establishment details where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, ordinary or group taxation status, consolidated tax group information, and relevant accounting regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL is normally taxable as a separate French corporate taxpayer. A non-resident parent is not included as the taxpayer unless a valid French tax consolidation election applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss reconciled to taxable profit or loss through permanent add-backs, tax deductions, exempt income, non-deductible expenses, depreciation adjustments, provisions, and other fiscal adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-head-office items that do not belong to the French entity, but include French-source expenses and transactions with non-resident related parties on an arm's-length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward or carried back, losses utilized during the year, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder's losses cannot be used directly against the SARL's taxable income. French loss rules apply at the company level, subject to statutory utilization limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2058-C-SD, Tax credits and distributable profit adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax-exempt amounts, participation-related adjustments, and other items affecting taxable profit or distributable results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the French company and retain supporting certificates, payroll records, expenditure schedules, and beneficiary documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of taxable, exempt, or preferentially taxed capital gains and losses, including disposals of fixed assets and qualifying securities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disposals involving a non-resident related party must be supported by valuation evidence and transfer-pricing documentation where the parties are associated enterprises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning ownership interests, subsidiaries, participations, and relevant related-party relationships.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign parent companies, ultimate beneficial owners where required, controlled entities, and material cross-border intra-group transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, applicable rate, corporate income tax due, credits, instalments, withholding offsets, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty or EU relief through the legally available withholding and refund procedures; do not net foreign taxes unless the relevant French tax-credit rules permit the offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalment amount, prior-year tax basis, applicable instalment percentage, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SARL remains responsible for instalments even where its parent or creditor is non-resident. Recalculate instalments after material changes in projected taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax liability, instalments already paid, credits, withholding offsets, and final balance or overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to the filed Form 2065 and accounting records. Refund claims require a French bank account or properly documented foreign payment instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of material transactions with associated enterprises, applicable transfer-pricing method, amounts, and documentation status, where filing thresholds and obligations are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border purchases, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and management charges involving the foreign parent or other group entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and relief provisions. Inaccurate returns may trigger reassessment, interest, tax penalties, and criminal proceedings in cases involving fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD, Corporate Income Tax Instalment Return and payment order, filed and paid electronically through the professional tax portal or approved electronic payment channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly, except where an exemption, low-liability threshold, new-company rule, or other statutory exception applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final instalment may be subject to a special percentage based on the preceding year's tax liability and the company's size or turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN number, tax period, legal name, and tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's identification details, not those of the foreign parent or foreign payment obligor.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate income tax liability or projected current-year liability used to calculate the instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign group tax amounts unless the French company is validly included in a French tax group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible tax credits and amounts already paid or credited against the instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only credits attributable to the French taxpayer and retain evidence of eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalment amount and electronic payment authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payer's bank mandate and French tax account are properly registered before the statutory due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally triggers a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Underpayment may also create a balancing payment and, in serious cases, additional penalties for inaccurate tax estimates or deliberate avoidance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, or a domestic exemption. The EU parent exemption generally requires qualifying ownership, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its competent foreign tax authority and documentation establishing beneficial ownership, entitlement to treaty benefits, ownership percentage, holding period, legal form, and absence of an abusive arrangement. The French payer should apply the reduced rate only where the applicable administrative procedure and documentation requirements are satisfied. Otherwise, the payer generally withholds at the domestic rate and the recipient files a refund claim with the French tax administration using the applicable treaty forms and supporting evidence. Principal-purpose, beneficial-ownership, anti-conduit, and anti-abuse requirements must be reviewed before relying on treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar remuneration paid to a non-resident are generally subject to 25% withholding tax under domestic law, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where applicable. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, although specific anti-abuse, non-cooperative-jurisdiction, deemed-distribution, or special-source rules may produce a different result. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income classification; the relevant treaty, beneficial-owner test, residence certificate, and anti-abuse provisions must be checked for each payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or belongs to a group meeting the statutory control or threshold conditions. A simplified documentation regime generally applies to other taxpayers engaged in controlled transactions, and materiality, audit, and disclosure requirements may still apply. A Country-by-Country Report is generally required for a qualifying multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. The annual transfer-pricing summary declaration, Form 2257-SD, may be required where statutory transaction and group thresholds are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single stand-alone economic substance regulation equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is enforced through general anti-abuse rules, the principal-purpose test in treaties, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, permanent-establishment principles, anti-hybrid rules, the abuse-of-law doctrine, and transfer-pricing rules. A French SARL performing runway paving should maintain genuine French personnel, management, equipment access, contracting authority, operational premises, banking, accounting, insurance, project records, and commercial risk commensurate with its reported profit. Artificial conduit arrangements, unsupported management fees, back-to-back financing, and profit allocation inconsistent with functions and risks are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing construction revenue, understating contract receipts, fabricating expenses, recording personal expenditure as project costs, or submitting knowingly false corporate income tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on conduct, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 500,000, with higher penalties in aggravated or organized cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director may incur criminal liability, personal tax liability in cases of fraudulent manoeuvres or serious and repeated non-compliance, civil restitution obligations, management bans, and asset seizure. A travel restriction is not automatic but may be ordered or imposed in criminal or enforcement proceedings; imprisonment is possible for proven tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Manipulation and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, procurement margins, financing costs, guarantees, or related-party subcontracting charges to shift runway-project profits outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under the arm's-length principle, denial of deductions, recharacterization as a hidden distribution, withholding tax exposure, late-payment interest, documentation penalties, and potential 40% or 80% penalties where deliberate or fraudulent conduct is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for intentional participation, fraudulent management, or serious repeated tax non-compliance. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced, but personal liability can arise under statutory tax-liability procedures, civil fault, criminal law, or insolvency proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing invoices for work not performed, manipulating reverse-charge treatment, claiming input VAT on fictitious subcontractors, or failing to account for VAT on taxable French construction supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input tax, late-payment interest, penalties generally up to 40% for deliberate conduct and up to 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct, and criminal prosecution for organized or aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be prosecuted personally where they authorized or knowingly facilitated false invoicing or VAT fraud. Civil tax-liability orders, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment may apply depending on the conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Artificial Residency, or Permanent-Establishment Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SARL without real operational capacity, booking contracts in France while all decision-making and execution occur abroad, or using a conduit company to obtain treaty or tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of the place of effective management or permanent establishment, French tax reassessment, withholding tax, penalties, interest, and possible abuse-of-law sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and criminal exposure if they knowingly created or operated an artificial arrangement. Travel bans or imprisonment are not automatic and require a competent authority's order or criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify or update the beneficial owner, accepting unexplained third-party payments, disguising the source of project funds, or using client-account structures to transfer illicit proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement, fines, account restrictions, transaction blocking, confiscation, professional sanctions, and criminal money-laundering penalties that may include imprisonment and substantial fines. Beneficial-owner filing failures may attract separate statutory fines and director liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, concealment, or negligent failure to implement required controls. Confiscation, civil restitution, management bans, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply according to the offense and judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery, Public Procurement, and Aviation-Infrastructure Corruption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering or accepting improper payments, commissions, gifts, sham consultancy fees, or political favors to obtain airport runway, civil aviation, or public works contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal bribery penalties, confiscation, exclusion from public procurement, debarment, contract invalidation, corporate fines, and possible compliance-monitoring measures. Accounting entries used to disguise bribes may create separate tax and false-accounting exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, employees, intermediaries, and beneficial owners may face individual criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, confiscation, management bans, and civil damages. Corporate limited liability does not protect a person who personally committed or authorized bribery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Labor, Payroll Tax, and Social Security Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared workers, fictitious subcontractors, false posted-worker documentation, concealed payroll, or arrangements intended to evade French social contributions and employment obligations on construction sites.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Backdated payroll taxes and social contributions, surcharges, labor-law fines, contract and procurement exclusion, site sanctions, and criminal penalties for concealed employment or illegal labor supply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director may be personally liable for concealed employment, unlawful subcontracting, worker safety failures, or contribution evasion. Civil compensation, management bans, asset seizure, and imprisonment may apply in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without required construction authorizations, ignoring airport safety controls, using non-compliant bitumen or asphalt materials, mishandling hazardous substances, or causing unlawful environmental damage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, suspension or withdrawal of authorization, remediation costs, environmental fines, contract termination, exclusion from public tenders, civil damages, and criminal penalties for serious safety or environmental offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and site managers may incur personal criminal or civil liability for knowing or negligent breaches, including bodily injury, death, pollution, or obstruction of regulators. Imprisonment and management bans may apply where statutory elements are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false accounts, concealing liabilities, inflating work-in-progress, diverting company assets, preferring related parties, or continuing operations while knowingly insolvent without proper action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of accounts, tax reassessment, civil damages, clawback of improper transactions, bankruptcy-related sanctions, personal liability for all or part of insufficient assets, and criminal penalties for fraudulent bankruptcy or false accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to the shortfall in company assets, prohibited from managing companies, required to restore diverted assets, and prosecuted criminally. Travel restrictions and imprisonment may occur only under applicable judicial or criminal procedures.
